ev: The design's own earlier sentence - that the post-merge uniqueness check does the failing - is refuted: gate::first_duplicate deliberately tolerates a repeated heading, so two sources declaring one source-only section passed silently unless a fact happened to sit inside; the gate cannot be the catcher because provenance is gone by then, and the fold still holds each source's tree.

The tolerance: gate.rs:64 fires only when a Fact sits on either side of the repeat, pinned by a_repeated_section_heading_is_not_flagged at gate.rs:131. The catcher: pipeline/fold.rs:173 first_source_section_collision, detector at :211, ordered as a fallback AFTER first_duplicate (:157) so a colliding fact still names its more specific id. The test: pipeline/collision_tests.rs:24, which asserts the failure with no fact present at all.

Judged fresh, and the judging found the refuted sentence still alive in two more homes than the design knew: the module header and the source-only append loop of merge.rs both still said the post-merge check catches it. Corrected in commit ca6411ff, which is what makes this fact's claim true of the whole tree rather than only of this document.

Node dedup and text dedup are different: the walker visits a shared source once, but the fold is textual inclusion, so in a diamond both parents inline the shared body and the seed carries it twice - harmless for prose and lethal for facts, hence an include guard admitting a node's body once by the first path in fold order.

The two mechanisms are distinct code: node dedup is the Color::Black short-circuit at use_graph.rs:112; the text guard is the `included` HashSet at pipeline/fold.rs:97, skipping at :140-141 and recording the first inline at :144, with the two reasons for skipping documented apart at :118-129. Tests: a_diamond_includes_the_shared_source_once at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:315 asserts exactly one copy, a_diamond_with_a_shared_fact_compiles at :353 is the lethal case, and source_fold_deduplicates_a_diamond at use_graph.rs:432 is the node half.

The fact's account of how it was found checks out against the test as it stands: the diamond test now asserts ONE copy, which is the post-guard state, and the design's 'first asserted two copies because that is what the code did' describes the measurement that produced the guard rather than the code today.
The lead line of the multi-source block, dating the shape to the owner's rulings of 2026-08-04 and the build to 2026-08-05.
Both dates resolve: BACKLOG.md ##B056-RULED carries the four rulings dated 2026-08-04, and the eight vibe-spec landings (87bb2bc8 through 5254f0cf) are all dated 2026-08-05 in git log.

A lead line asserts only that the block below it exists and is dated; both halves are checkable and both check, so it is confirmed rather than unverifiable. The six numbered facts it introduces are judged individually below.
A contract may declare more than one #source and every one is honoured in declaration order; before this the compiler took the first and dropped the rest without a word.

use_graph.rs:196 source_addresses iterates every DirectiveKind::Source (:201-204) and flattens the expansions in place (:192-195); the fold hands the full member slice to fold_sources (pipeline/fold.rs:130-151). Tests: two_sources_both_folded_in_declaration_order at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:88, sources_fold_in_declaration_order_not_alphabetical at :120, no_source_directive_lines_remain_with_two_sources at :251.

The 'before this' half is measurable and measured: the pre-B-056 selector `.find(|d| d.kind == DirectiveKind::Source)` returns zero hits over crates/vibe-spec/src, so the silence B-055 recorded has no remaining site.
:replace from any source discards the contract text only, the sources still sum among themselves in order, and with one source the result is byte-identical to the prior single-source behaviour.

merge.rs:197-199 any_replace over the members; merge.rs:200-203 drops the contract text and emits every member in slice order. Backward compatibility is structural rather than asserted: fold_source delegates to fold_sources(c, &[s]) at merge.rs:242-244, and fold_source_equals_fold_sources_singleton at merge.rs:484 byte-compares the paths. Tests: fold_sources_replace_on_second_keeps_both_sources at merge.rs:421 and replace_in_second_source_drops_contract_keeps_both_sources at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:149.
The owner's reformulation is what the code implements: there is no arbitration between two :replace sources anywhere in the fold, because any() collapses the question before the branch is taken.

A contract fact is dropped when ANY member of S(a) redeclares its id, and two sources redeclaring one id is not a fold question because both survive into the merged text and the uniqueness recheck fails loudly.

merge.rs:142-158 overridden_facts collects the source ids as a union (:147-151) and drops the contract facts whose id is in it (:152-157), applied at :207; the surviving-duplicate half is gate.rs:54 first_duplicate. Tests: fold_sources_add_union_of_overridden_facts at merge.rs:438 for the union, a_fact_duplicate_between_two_sources_fails_the_build at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:182 for the loud failure.

This fact leans on the post-merge gate and the lean is sound, unlike the neighbouring source-only case: a doubly-redeclared FACT puts a Fact node on either side of the repeat, which is exactly the condition gate.rs:64 fires on.

A source-only section declared by two sources is an error, and where it is caught matters: the post-merge check sees provenance-free text and tolerates a repeated heading, so the collision is judged in the fold, which still knows which source brought what.

pipeline/fold.rs:173 first_source_section_collision -> CompileError::DuplicateSourceSection (pipeline.rs:60-66), detector at pipeline/fold.rs:211 with the two-or-more test at :243, deliberately placed after first_duplicate (:157). The tolerance that forces it there: gate.rs:64, pinned by gate.rs:131. Tests: pipeline/collision_tests.rs:24 (no fact inside, still fails), :61 (matching a contract anchor stays a legal :add), :113 (an inner-level collision names the inner node).

The asymmetry the fact calls deliberate is implemented as an asymmetry rather than described as one: a source section matching a contract anchor takes the sum branch, and only a section the contract never declared reaches the collision detector.

The fold follows #source recursively under the section 9 cycle law and carries an include guard; a contract cycle is legal and contributes nothing not yet folded, a cycle touching an implementation is a build error naming the path, and it is the same walker with one more edge set rather than a second traversal.

Recursion: fold_source_closure at pipeline/fold.rs:65 over source_fold_order (use_graph.rs:84), which is the shared visit (:102) under EdgeKind::Source. Cycle law: use_graph.rs:120 admits a loop whose nodes are all contracts, :123-125 raises UseGraphError::Cycle otherwise, is_contract at :223. Include guard at pipeline/fold.rs:97/:140-141/:144. Tests: a_source_cycle_between_contracts_compiles at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:392, a_source_cycle_through_an_impl_fails at :413, a_diamond_includes_the_shared_source_once at :315, source_edges_and_use_edges_do_not_mix at use_graph.rs:526.

One cosmetic divergence measured and judged not to touch the claim: the error's Display reads 'use cycle: ...' even for a #source cycle, because one Display serves both EdgeKinds (use_graph.rs:30). The fact promises the path be named, and the path IS named correctly; only the generic word 'use' is imprecise. Recorded as a wording defect, not a behavioural one.

A #source address may carry a * in the package-NAME half; it names every installed package whose name matches AND that carries the addressed document, expanded sorted; an empty match is a legal empty set while a pointed address still fails loudly; and both the fold and the cycle guard read a document's #source edges through one function.

resolver/glob.rs:47 is_pattern (name half only), :60 expand_pattern with the slot scan (:84), name match (:141), membership requiring both name and document (:121-128), sort (:109) and dedup (:113); a non-pattern returns itself (:68-70) and an empty match returns Ok(vec![]). Loud pointed failure: resolver.rs:126-130 PatternNotExpanded, plus Unresolved from visit at use_graph.rs:133-138. The one edge reader: use_graph.rs:196 source_addresses, called by the guard at :168 and by the fold at pipeline/fold.rs:130. Tests: resolver/glob.rs:264, :330, :396, :458, and the_fold_reaches_a_source_through_a_glob_expanded_edge at pipeline/tests.rs:444.

The last clause is the one worth having judged, because its failure would be silent: a glob expanded one way for the guard and another for the fold would build a guard over a graph the fold never walks. Both call the same function, and pipeline/tests.rs:444 exercises the agreement end to end rather than asserting it structurally.
